paper.title_en: Systematic study of fully heavy-flavored tetraquarks \(Q_{1}Q_{2}{\overline{Q}}_{1}{\overline{Q}}_{2}\) (\(Q_{1,2} \in \{ b,c\}\)): Mass spectra, threshold analysis, and confrontation with LHC data
paper.abstract_en: Experimental searches for fully heavy flavored tetraquark states are actively pursued at the LHC. The LHCb, CMS, and ATLAS collaborations have investigated fully charmed <math display="inline"><mi>c</mi><mi>c</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math>, doubly charmed-bottom <math display="inline"><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> and fully bottom <math display="inline"><mi>b</mi><mi>b</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> tetraquarks. Fully charmed states are probed as intermediate resonances in processes like <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></math> and <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> at <math display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></math>, and 13 TeV. Notably, narrow structures such as <math display="inline"><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6200</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, <math display="inline"><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6900</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>, and <math display="inline"><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7300</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> observed in the di-<math display="inline"><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></math> mass spectrum have ignited theoretical interest. In this study, we use a nonrelativistic model to perform a detailed study of the mass spectra for the ground (<math display="inline"><mn>1</mn><mi>S</mi></math>) and excited (<math display="inline"><mn>1</mn><mi>P</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><mn>2</mn><mi>S</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><mn>1</mn><mi>D</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><mn>2</mn><mi>P</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><mn>3</mn><mi>S</mi></math>, and <math display="inline"><mn>4</mn><mi>S</mi></math>) states of fully heavy tetraquarks <math display="inline"><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></math> <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> in the diquark-antiquark picture. Tetraquarks are modeled as color-singlet bound states build from an axial-vector diquark (<math display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>) and axial-vector antidiquark (<math display="inline"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>) in the <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mn mathvariant="bold">3</mn><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> and <math display="inline"><mrow><mn mathvariant="bold">3</mn></mrow></math> color representations, respectively, bound together by color forces. With this setup, the Schrödinger equation is solved numerically for a modified version of the Cornell potential, using the three-point difference central method. The spin-dependent terms are dealt with nonperturbatively and are used to describe the splitting structure of the diquark. The tetraquark states are investigated for a wide range of <math display="inline"><msup><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>P</mi><mi>C</mi></mrow></msup></math> quantum numbers including <math display="inline"><msup><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> for <math display="inline"><mi>S</mi></math>-waves, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mo>±</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mo>±</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> for <math display="inline"><mi>P</mi></math>-waves, and <math display="inline"><msup><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>±</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>±</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>±</mo></mrow></msup></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>+</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> for <math display="inline"><mi>D</mi></math>-waves. Following the same line as many previous works, we attempt, through this study of tetraquark mass spectra, to provide their possible signatures in narrow structures recently discovered in the di-<math display="inline"><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></math> production spectrum by the LHCb, CMS, and ATLAS collaborations. Our results provide precise mass predictions, analyze stability against strong fall-apart decays, and are directly compared with recent LHC observations and other relevant theoretical models. Our findings supports the interpretation of these discovered exotic heavy resonances as the different excitations of the fully charmed tetraquark, offering a crucial guide for ongoing experimental identification.
